# Anthropics børsbombe og politisk kaos i Israel

**Feed**: store-penge  
**Published**: 2026-10-29  
**Market Sentiment**: Mixed

⏱️ **Time Horizon Key**: ST = <3 months | MT = 3-12 months | LT = >12 months

---

## Episode Thesis

This Danish Store Penge episode starts by mocking ATP's weak result: its 2026 return fell from 14.5% after six months to 1.5% after nine. Most of the episode is about the AI capex race. Hosts and guest are bullish on AI infrastructure suppliers such as SK Hynix, Vertiv, Celestica and Cadence. They are more cautious on hyperscalers like Meta, which are funding capex with debt and new shares that dilute existing shareholders. They also discuss Anthropic's IPO prospectus, the Israeli election, and an expected US stock rally plus Iran escalation after the midterms. They call themselves bullish on stocks after the midterm election.

---

## Universe Stocks

### 🟢 VRT — Vertiv | **BUY** (Moderate)

**Sentiment**: Positive | **Time Horizon**: MT  
**Confidence**: 60%

Datacenter cooling supplier up ~15% on strong report; Mikkel says the money is in datacenter builders and suppliers first.

#### Reasoning

Guest Mikkel Rosenvold's view, with host Tobias Storm agreeing: the AI infrastructure supply chain (datacenter builders, chips, power supply, energy) will benefit first. Vertiv's full order books and strong report support this. Mikkel sees a lot of money to be made over 1-2 years for those who can stomach the volatility.

#### Sell Triggers

- if Korean export data or chip spot prices roll over
- if hyperscalers cut AI capex
- if Anthropic/OpenAI revenue growth stalls

> *"Så start helt nede i dem, der smider datacenter op, dem der leverer chipsene lidt højere op, dem der leverer strømforsyningen til dem"*

---

### 🟢 000660.KS — SK Hynix | **BUY** (Moderate)

**Sentiment**: Positive | **Time Horizon**: MT  
**Confidence**: 60%

Record report with +32% QoQ revenue; chip/memory suppliers are where AI money lies; market prices in falling memory prices but not rising earnings.

#### Reasoning

Mikkel argues that stock prices already reflect falling memory and chip prices, but not the big rise in earnings and demand. Chip suppliers sit low in the AI chain, which he thinks benefits first. SK Hynix's record quarter supports this.

#### Sell Triggers

- if South Korean export figures disappoint
- if memory/chip spot prices roll over
- if rates keep rising and risk budgets shrink

> *"Men det er ikke priset ind, at indtjeningen også stiger, og efterspørgselen stiger helt enormt."*

---

### 🟡 META — Meta | **HOLD** (Weak)

**Sentiment**: Mixed | **Time Horizon**: LT  
**Confidence**: 50%

Strong AI case, but up to $100bn share issuance dilutes holders; Mikkel expects Mag7 to rise only after the case is proven.

#### Reasoning

Mikkel thinks hyperscalers like Meta will rise eventually, but only after they get past the financing hump and show AI profits. Until then, dilution from heavy share issuance and borrowing weighs on the stock even though the business case is good. Tobias notes Meta trades at a far lower P/E than Anthropic.

#### Sell Triggers

- if AI capex proves unprofitable
- if dilution from share issuance accelerates

> *"Så MAC7-selskaberne, Meta og sådan nogle, skal nok komme til at stige, men det tror jeg først kommer, når det her virkelig er bevist."*

---

### 🟠 GOOGL — Alphabet (Google) | **WATCH** (Weak)

**Sentiment**: Positive | **Time Horizon**: MT  
**Confidence**: 50%

Tobias thinks Google will catch up in AI given unlimited spend and trades at a much lower P/E than Anthropic; cloud results due tonight.

#### Reasoning

Tobias is more skeptical of Anthropic at $1.5-2tn because Google and Meta have committed to spend whatever it takes, will likely catch up, and are much cheaper on P/E. He is watching Alphabet's cloud growth and margins in tonight's report.

#### Sell Triggers

- if cloud growth or compute profitability disappoints

> *"Så jeg tror, at Google og Meta, der jo også er i samme boldgade, ja, de kommer jo nok til at catche op, og de handler i hvert fald til en langt lavere price-earning ratio"*

---
